reasons.specificity: The inventory closely tracks Deutschmann’s distinct money-capital process, Schumpeterian temporary rents, communicative myth diffusion, institutionalization, lock-in, and conditional terminal scenario.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly all substantive edges and qualifications are supported by accurate quotations, though the isolated globalization-to-unpredictability edge compresses the source’s broader plural cause, “these developments.”
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes processual capital from stocks, closure at the class of myths from recurrence of one technology, and an explicitly named “spiral” from a demonstrated feedback loop.
reasons.coherence: The main tables consistently separate source claims, reconstructions, and hypotheses, but the scope assessment contradicts its claimed complete review and refers to nonexistent V.F findings and a purported malformed F6.
reasons.usefulness: The stocks/flows inventory and edge table are highly usable with the text open, especially because signs, unknown delays, open edges, replacement closure, and evidentiary status are explicit.
reasons.hallucination_risk: The substantive dynamics are mostly bounded and faithful, but the final audit metadata invents retained findings V.F1–V.F3 and an F6 repeated-field defect that are absent from the displayed ledger.

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: The scope assessment says added findings “V.F1,” “V.F2,” and “V.F3” were retained and that ledger row F6 has repeated anchor fields.
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The displayed findings ledger contains only F1–F22, with no V.F entries, and F6 contains a single anchor field: “then he enjoys a temporary monopoly, on which the entrepreneurial profit and the growth of the economy are based.”

score.one_line: An excellent, source-specific dynamics inventory undermined mainly by hallucinated and internally inconsistent scope-audit metadata.
